botany.native_range: South America, principally south-eastern Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina and Uruguay. It is widely planted far outside its native range, including across the subtropics.
botany.habitat: Open woodland and forest margins on well-drained ground; very widely planted as an ornamental street and campus tree.
botany.climate: Subtropical to tropical, with a mild or dry winter. Frost tolerance is poor.
distinguishing_characteristics: Bipinnate, fern-like leaves in pairs along slender twigs.
Showy tubular violet-blue flowers, produced in profusion before the leaves in many climates.
A rounded, spreading crown on a short trunk, often with several heavy limbs.
Long, flat, brown seed pods that hang through the winter.
interesting_facts: Flowering is often spectacular enough that cities call the bloom a 'jacaranda cloud'.
The genus name honours Francisco Hernando de Jacaranda, an early-eighteenth-century naval officer.
As with many members of Bignoniaceae, the seed pods are long and contain winged seeds.
botany.attribution: Botanical summary compiled for Arboretum. Verify against the Kew Plants of the World Online record for Jacaranda mimosifolia before treating any specific figure as authoritative.
